summary: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the LIFO principle. Operations on a stack include push, which adds an element to the top, pop, which removes the top element, and peek, which returns the top element without removing it. Attempting to pop from an empty stack is known as stack underflow.

key_terms.definition: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the LIFO principle.
A principle where the last element added is the first one out, which a stack follows.
Push adds an element to the top of the stack.
Pop removes the element from the top of the stack.
Peek returns the top element without removing it.
Stack underflow is what happens when you try to pop from an empty stack.
